newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RESEARCH ALERT - Alpargatas initiated, Disco cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Alpargatas initiated, Disco cut.

text.p: -- Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Friday announced it initiated coverage of Argentina's textile and footwear company Alpargatas with a hold rating.

-- Topper brand (34 percent of footwear sales and 22 percent of total sales) should begin penetration in the new Central American market during 1997, analyst Eduardo Pellagatta wrote in a report. The estimated size of the market is $800 million, he added.

-- If Alpargatas manages to sell $40 million in assets over 1997, issue $60 million in capital and cancel debt during the first quarter of 1997, it will reduce interest costs by an estimated $3 million in fiscal 1997. It has $91 million in debt coming due in the period.
-- Fiscal year 1997 cash flow should be negative $70 million, therefore the asset sale plan and a capital increase are necessary steps unless the company plans to further increase its debt level.

-- Analyst Carlos de Leon said DMG was downgrading Argentina's supermarket chain Disco to hold from buy given the strong performance. It has risen by 68.2 percent since its IPO in April 1996, outperforming the market by 27.8 percent over this period.
-- "Our earnings forecast remain unchanged at $19.2 million for FY96 and $24.2 million for FY97, which are in line with consensus estimates".
-- De Leon added DMG recommends short-term investors to take profits in Argentina's Juan Minetti and to switch into local firm Corcemar, both of them cement firms.
-- "Corcemar is trading on a P/BV (price/book value) of 0.9x and FV/t (firm value/per tonne of capacity) of $156, 25 percent below the Latin American average.

-- "Minetti looks expensive on a 1997 P/E (price/earnings ratio) of 24.4x, P/CF (price/cash flow ratio) of 11.8x and FV/EBIDTA (firm value/earnings before interest and taxes ratio) of 9.2x but also on a P/BV of 1.3x and FV/t of $198."
